_comment: THE LOAD TEST'S LIMITS (DECISIONS #284; tests/load_test.sh, tools/load/load_test.py). A step of the test HOLDS when every limit here holds; the first step that does not is where the game breaks on this machine. A limit of null is measured and reported but not judged. A genre may override any of them in shared/<genre>/load.json (later genres win). The 'keeps up' limits are engineering facts: the movement tick runs 20 times a second, so a tick that takes longer than its 50 ms falls behind. The per-client bandwidth limits are a design budget (Luke's to set: null until he does). 'referee_gone_refusals' counts judged abilities refused because the referee had dropped out. 'level' is the level world 0 plays the test on (a LevelDef id; 0 the greybox): a game whose world is elsewhere sets it in its own load.json. 'referees' [columns, rows] cuts the bots' square into that many regions, a referee each (DECISIONS #288); [1, 1] is one referee for the whole world.
